title: gov.uk: relief at source adds 20% and net pay takes the contribution before tax, so 5% of £40,000 costs £1,600 either way; salary sacrifice also saves 8% National Insurance
working: 2,000 x 20% = 400 of tax relief under each. Salary sacrifice also saves 2,000 x 8% = 160 of National Insurance: 2,000 - 400 - 160 = 1,440.

title: gov.uk: a higher rate taxpayer gets 40% relief; 8% of £60,000 costs £2,880 with relief at source or net pay, and salary sacrifice also lowers National Insurance and Plan 2 repayments
working: 4,800 x 40% = 1,920 of tax relief (20% claimed by the provider and 20% through the wider basic rate band under relief at source). Sacrifice: 4,800 x 2% = 96 of National Insurance; loan 9% of 30,615 = 2,755 against 9% of 25,815 = 2,323, saving 432. 4,800 - 1,920 - 96 - 432 = 2,352.

title: gov.uk: pension contributions reduce adjusted net income, so 10% of £110,000 brings it to £99,000 and restores the full personal allowance
working: Tax on 110,000: allowance 7,570, taxable 102,430, 7,540 + 64,730 x 40% = 33,432. On 99,000: allowance 12,570, taxable 86,430, 27,032. Saved 6,400. Relief at source: 2,200 claimed by the provider and tax falls to 9,740 + 48,730 x 40% = 29,232, 4,200 less. Sacrifice also saves 11,000 x 2% = 220.

title: gov.uk rates: 3% of £20,000 is £600, costing £480 after 20% relief and £432 under salary sacrifice
